name: The fifteen limbs of the Aparokṣānubhūti (pañcadaśāṅga-yoga)

stages.name: yama
stages.description: control of the senses through knowing 'all is Brahman'

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: constant flow of like thoughts (of Brahman), excluding others

stages.name: tyāga
stages.description: abandoning the world of appearances by seeing it as consciousness

stages.name: mauna
stages.description: that from which words turn back: abiding in it

stages.name: deśa
stages.description: the 'place' where there is no people at beginning, middle or end — Brahman

stages.name: kāla
stages.description: the indivisible Brahman in which all time arises

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: that in which one can meditate on Brahman uninterruptedly with ease

stages.name: mūla-bandha
stages.description: Brahman, the root of all beings, in which the mind is restrained

stages.name: deha-sāmya
stages.description: absorption in the uniform Brahman, not mere straightness of body

stages.name: dṛk-sthiti
stages.description: seeing the world as Brahman, not gazing at the nose-tip

stages.name: prāṇa-saṃyamana
stages.description: negation of the world (exhalation), 'I am Brahman' (inhalation), steadiness in it (retention)

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: seeing the self in all objects, merging the mind in consciousness

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: holding the mind on Brahman wherever it goes

stages.name: ātma-dhyāna
stages.description: the unsupported state 'I am Brahman alone'

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: the mode's changeless, distinction-free identity with Brahman, forgetting all modes

notes: Order and glosses from memory (moderate); verse numbers low. The text says haṭha-yoga combined with this is for the unripe; for the ripe this alone suffices (vv. c. 143–144). Bands are interpretive.

name: The seven states of the jīva (Pañcadaśī 7)

stages.name: ajñāna
stages.description: not knowing the self (the ten men not counting themselves)

stages.name: āvaraṇa
stages.description: 'the tenth is not there, it does not shine'

stages.name: vikṣepa
stages.description: grief, wrong notions ('the tenth is lost')

stages.name: parokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: 'there is a tenth' — knowledge from the teacher's word not yet one's own

stages.name: aparokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: 'you are the tenth' — recognizing oneself as Brahman

stages.name: śoka-nivṛtti
stages.description: grief ends with recognition

stages.name: niraṅkuśa-tṛpti
stages.description: the satisfaction of one who has done all that is to be done (jīvanmukti)

notes: Illustrated by the tenth-man story. Bands are interpretive.

name: Hearing to nirvikalpa samādhi with eight auxiliaries (Vedāntasāra)

sources.ref: sections on the means and samādhi

stages.name: adhikāra
stages.description: purification through duties; the four means

stages.name: śravaṇa
stages.description: determining the purport by the six marks

stages.name: manana
stages.description: reasoning in accord with the teaching

stages.name: yama–dhāraṇā
stages.description: restraint, observance, posture, breath control, withdrawal, holding

stages.name: nididhyāsana / dhyāna
stages.description: flow of like ideas excluding unlike

stages.name: savikalpa-samādhi
stages.description: mode rests in Brahman, knower–known distinction remaining

stages.name: nirvikalpa-samādhi
stages.description: like salt dissolved in water; overcoming laya, vikṣepa, kaṣāya, rasāsvāda

stages.name: jīvanmukti
stages.description: abiding as Brahman with the body sustained by prārabdha

notes: Bands are interpretive; the Vedāntasāra itself treats samādhi as a means to the knowledge that liberates.

name: The path of the gods (arcirādi-mārga) in the Brahma Sūtras

stages.name: utkrānti
stages.description: speech merges in mind, mind in breath, breath in the self; the meditator departs by the channel beyond the hundred (crown)

stages.name: arcis
stages.description: first station of the path, 'that being well known'

stages.name: ahar, śukla-pakṣa, uttarāyaṇa, saṃvatsara
stages.gloss: day, bright fortnight, northern course, year
stages.description: stations of the path (listed in the Upaniṣads; ordered by BS 4.3.2–3)

stages.name: vāyu, āditya, candra, vidyut
stages.description: further stations; the stations are deities who conduct the soul (ātivāhika)

stages.name: amānava puruṣa (with Varuṇa, Indra, Prajāpati)
stages.description: from lightning a non-human person leads the soul on to Brahman

stages.name: brahmaloka
stages.description: for Bādari and Śaṅkara, the conditioned Brahman

stages.name: kāryātyaye mokṣa
stages.gloss: liberation at the dissolution of that world
stages.description: with its ruler, beyond it; no return

notes: An eschatological route rather than a meditative ladder; bands left empty for the stations. Station order recalled with moderate confidence. Advaita: this path is only for meditators on the qualified Brahman; the knower of the attributeless does not depart.
